state:
- The Phase-2 sufficiency arm has an attribution confound: recruiting a promiscuous proline-directed kinase (CDK5/p38) to the nuclear envelope will phosphorylate many NE-proximal substrates, so import failure there cannot be attributed to NUP98 even with site occupancy confirmed. Fix by crossing the arms: show phospho-null (S-to-A) knock-in neurons at Phase-1-confirmed sites are resistant to kinase-recruitment-induced import failure, which would isolate NUP98 as the relevant substrate.
- Target selection for NUP98 rests entirely on unverified external knowledge (mitotic phosphosites); the packet never singles out NUP98 over other FG-nucleoporins (NUP62, NUP153, NUP93). Fix by pre-registering a broad FG-Nup panel in the Phase-1 phosphoproteomics so a negative finding on NUP98 routes the hypothesis to the next candidate rather than killing the whole class, and by citing S1's aggregate proteomics specifically if NUP98 appears in it.
- The proposed mechanism bundles two distinct lesions ('weakens NUP98 attachment to the pore scaffold' and 'destabilizes the FG permeability barrier') without a designed discriminator between them, and the temporal acceptance criterion imports RanGAP mislocalization from the C9orf72 context [S2] into the TDP-43-positive context. Fix by naming a scaffold-vs-barrier readout (e.g., scaffold-anchored vs FG-permeability-specific assays at confirmed sites) and defining TDP-43-context-specific temporal landmarks instead of borrowing S2's.
